claims.text: HfZrTiTa0.53 is an equiatomic high-entropy alloy.
As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 has a mixed microstructure consisting primarily of BCC material with residual HCP and omega-phase precipitates.
The omega-phase precipitates in as-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 are brittle and deleterious.
Annealing HfZrTiTa0.53 at approximately 950°C for 1 hour in argon followed by controlled cooling will reduce or dissolve residual omega phase.
The proposed annealing treatment will produce a more uniformly distributed BCC matrix.
The proposed annealing treatment will alleviate segregation-related microstructural inhomogeneities.
Reducing omega precipitates and microstructural inhomogeneity will reduce sites for premature crack initiation.
A more homogeneous microstructure will promote uniform dislocation glide during tensile loading.
More uniform dislocation glide will delay tensile strain localization.
The annealed alloy will have greater room-temperature tensile ductility than the as-cast alloy.
The annealed alloy will have greater uniform tensile elongation and a more uniform tensile strain distribution than the as-cast alloy.
The proposed treatment will cause little to no reduction in compressive strength.
A predominant stabilized BCC phase will continue to support high strength after annealing.
As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 exhibits rapid impact-triggered oxidation energy release.
The annealed alloy will retain a dynamic energy-release response similar to that of the as-cast alloy.
The limited tensile ductility of as-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 is caused by brittle omega precipitates and microstructural inhomogeneities.
SHPB compression at approximately 4000 s^-1 in air, combined with spark intensity and ignition-time imaging, can evaluate oxidation-based dynamic energy release.
The hypothesis is limited to room-temperature quasi-static tension and high-strain-rate compression near 4000 s^-1 in air.

contradictions.description: The alloy is called equiatomic, but HfZrTiTa0.53 specifies a Ta atomic ratio of 0.53 relative to 1 for each other element and therefore is not equiatomic.
